chapter.title: Configuration
chapter.para: JetOS has no run-time configuration: a module is described once, in a configuration file in the XML format of ARINC 653 part 1, and the kernel is built for that description.

section.para: JetOS shall take the configuration of the module, that is its partitions, their memory, the schedule, the ports and the channels between them, and the health monitoring tables, from a description that is fixed when it is built.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A fixed configuration is what makes the behaviour of the module predictable and certifiable.

section.para: JetOS shall not change the configuration of the module while it runs.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A fixed configuration is what makes the behaviour of the module predictable and certifiable.

section.para: The schedule of a module shall be an ordered list of slots.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The slots are what the time partitioning is made of.

section.para: The duration of a slot of the schedule shall be at least 1 millisecond.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A shorter slot would be ended by the next tick of the timer before its partition could do any work.

formalpara.title: Traceability
formalpara.para: Not applicable: a constraint on the configuration, which the configuration tool checks when the module is built; no function of the kernel implements it.

section.para: The length of a major frame shall be the sum of the durations of its slots.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The slots are what the time partitioning is made of.

section.para: The kind of a slot of the schedule shall be partition, spare, monitor, GDB or networking.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The slots are what the time partitioning is made of.

section.para: JetOS shall be built only from a configuration in which: the first slot belongs to a partition; every partition has at least one slot in which its periodic processing may start; a slot for networking is present if and only if networking is configured; the memory blocks mapped into one partition do not share pages; names that identify partitions, ports and memory blocks are unique when compared without regard to case; and the sizes of the messages of the two ends of a channel agree.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: An inconsistent configuration is found when the module is built, not when it flies.

section.para: JetOS shall treat names of partitions, processes, ports and memory blocks as equal when they differ only in case.
The configuration shall give each partition: a name, an identifier, a period (the major frame if none is given), the size of its memory, its ports, and its health monitoring table.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: These are the properties of a partition that the kernel needs to schedule it and to give it memory.

section.para: The configuration shall tell for each partition whether it is a kernel-only partition.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The kernel-only partitions (the monitor, the GDB server) are set up by the kernel, not loaded from an image.

section.para: The configuration shall give the module a health monitoring table, and each partition one, mapping a system state and an error to an action.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The default is the safe side of each level.

section.para: The action for an entry that is missing in a health monitoring table shall be shutting down the module for the module table and idling the partition for a partition table.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The default is the safe side of each level.
